scenario: Young woman with two days of burning urine and frequency; likely simple UTI; cotrimoxazole rash.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Hello, Priya. Come in. How can I help?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Hello doctor. Sorry, the air conditioner outside is so cold, I am shivering a bit. Doctor, it burns when I pass urine, and I have to go again and again.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: How many days has this been going on?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Two days. It started the day before yesterday, in the evening.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Any fever, chills, pain in the sides or back? Any blood in the urine?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No fever. No pain in the sides. But I am not sure about the blood, the urine looked a bit pink once, or maybe it was the beetroot I ate.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Alright. Any discharge, or any chance that you are pregnant?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: No discharge. My period was two weeks back, normal. No chance, I think.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Have you had this before?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Yes, I had a urine infection last year, in July. I took antibiotics directly from the chemist, and it went away.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: And are you taking any regular medicines? Any allergies?

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Only cetirizine at night, for my dust allergy. And, um, cotrimoxazole gave me a rash once, so I do not take that.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Thank you. Your temperature is 98.4, blood pressure is 110 over 70, and pulse is 84.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: That is fine, no? Doctor, I am worried it has gone to my kidneys. My aunt had kidney stones and she was in a lot of pain.

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Let me examine you. There is mild tenderness just above the pubic bone, but there is no tenderness in the loin, so the kidneys look fine.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: So what is it?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Most likely a urinary tract infection, a simple one.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: What test is needed?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: A urine test today, and I will send a urine culture also, so we know which germ it is.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: And the medicines?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Nitrofurantoin 100 milligrams twice a day with food for five days. Drink plenty of water, three litres a day, and do not hold your urine.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay. Can I take something if it burns a lot?

turns.speaker: Doctor
turns.text: Paracetamol is fine for the discomfort. If you get fever or back pain, or the burning is not better in three days, come back the same day. Otherwise see me when the culture report is ready.

turns.speaker: Patient
turns.text: Okay doctor, thank you.

gold.key: had a urine infection last year
worried it has gone to my kidneys
mild tenderness just above the pubic bone
see me when the culture report is ready

notes: The cold air-conditioner remark in turn 1 is small talk (the chief complaint in the same turn is labelled). Turn 5 has an ambiguous finding (pink urine, or maybe beetroot) labelled uncertain. The period remark and the vague no chance, I think in turn 7 are not labelled. Turn 9 mentions antibiotics from the chemist with no drug name, so there is no medication_history row. Turn 11 has a drug reaction (cotrimoxazole rash) plus an environmental allergy (dust) and a regular medicine (cetirizine). Turn 22 lists return-early triggers (fever, back pain) that are advice, not reported symptoms, and are not labelled as symptoms. The patient takes cetirizine; the doctor prescribes nitrofurantoin (different) and advises paracetamol.
